intro_html: Takeout-style lo mein with a honey soy sriracha sauce, a mountain of vegetables, and lean turkey doing the protein work. Every serving lands 43 grams of protein for about $5.57 a bowl (at everyday cost). The delivery app cannot touch those macros or that price.
cost_closing_html: About $5.57 a bowl (at everyday cost) for lo mein a takeout counter sells for $12 a container, with maybe half the meat and none of the leftovers.
shop_smart: The lo mein noodles are the shocker at $9.92 for two packs. Plain spaghetti pulls the same duty in a stir fry for about $2, and it would knock more than 50 cents off every bowl.
Cabbage is the cheapest vegetable in the cart: 59 cents of a $1.57 head fills nearly 5 cups of this batch.
This uses 5.5 lb of turkey, so buy the big 6 lb pack. The per-pound savings over small trays covers the mushrooms.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce: honey, soy sauce, sriracha, hoisin, and ground ginger. Set it by the stove.
Boil the lo mein noodles 1 minute short of the package time, drain, and rinse briefly so they do not clump.
Heat half the olive oil in your biggest pot or wok. Brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and stir fry the carrots, onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms until they just soften, about 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and spinach and cook 2 more minutes.
Return the turkey, add the noodles and sauce, and toss over high heat until everything is coated and glossy.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each container and every bowl comes out to about 565 calories and 43 grams of protein.

steps: Whisk honey, soy sauce, sriracha, hoisin, and ginger into a sauce.
Boil the noodles just shy of package time and drain.
Brown the turkey to 165F in oil, then set aside and stir fry the vegetables.
Toss turkey, noodles, and sauce together over high heat and portion into 14 containers.
